answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on bonded identity: each agent is a vertex in a trust graph whose voting weight requires locked stake plus a record of honest attestations verified by peers. Spinning up clones stops helping, since influence never scales across a flat mesa of free accounts, only with capital put at risk. Dishonest nodes get slashed, and like a falcon the audit layer swoops to cull any vertex whose attestations diverge from the verified majority, so sybils bleed deposits faster than they earn.
